text:
[title] Block tables
[body] KV-cache split into fixed-size blocks, mapped per sequence
[body] Copy-on-write shares blocks across parallel samples
[body] Prefix caching hit rate: 61% on the chat workload

novice.takeaway: The slide describes a memory management technique that splits and shares cached data in blocks to improve efficiency, backed by a 61% cache hit rate.
questions: What is KV-cache in this context?
What counts as a 'prefix caching hit'?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe this block-based caching method contributes to the earlier 2.4x efficiency gain.

peer.takeaway: A block-based memory management scheme divides the KV-cache into fixed blocks, enabling sharing across samples and cache reuse to improve efficiency.
questions: How does prefix caching relate to block tables?
Why does 61% hit rate matter for throughput?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe this block table design efficiently manages memory to boost throughput.

expert.takeaway: The slide describes PagedAttention-style block table management (fixed-size blocks, copy-on-write, prefix caching) as a mechanism enabling the earlier claimed efficiency gains.
questions: Is 61% hit rate representative or best-case?
How does this interact with speculative decoding from slide 3?
expert.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe block-table-based memory management is key to the serving system's efficiency.

metrics.intent: Our serving system delivers 2.4x higher goodput at p99 latency by pairing PagedAttention-style KV-cache management with speculative decoding.
